intro: If you've been searching for cloudflare pages free tier, you've probably noticed two kinds of advice: paid tools that open with a soft upsell, and abandoned blog posts that stopped being true years ago. This one is built to stay useful, and it's maintained automatically.

We'll walk through Cloudflare Pages, Github Pages, Is-a.dev Free Domains, and Automate the boring parts — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Cloudflare Pages
paragraphs: Start with the basics. Cloudflare Pages is a free static hosting platform with a global CDN and preview deploys for every pull request.

In practice that means: Connect a Git repo and every branch or PR gets its own preview URL, while the main branch gets a production URL on Cloudflare's network. The free tier covers static sites comfortably and custom domains are supported without a separate CDN bill.
No signup wall, no credit card — just a README and some patience.
bullets: Create a Pages project in the Cloudflare dashboard and link the repo
Point the build output at the static folder
Add a custom domain in the project's domains tab

sections.heading: Github Pages
paragraphs: Start with the basics. GitHub Pages is a free static-hosting service built directly into the repo that already hosts your code.

The upshot: Point Pages at any subdirectory of a repository and GitHub serves it over HTTPS with a built-in URL, custom domain support, and automatic deploys on every push. For a static blog the entire hosting bill is zero, with no server, no DNS glue, and no renewal dates.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.
bullets: Pick a directory (e.g. autopilot-blog/site/) as the site source in repo Settings → Pages
Push (or let the engine push) the built HTML and the site deploys in under a minute
Optionally map a custom domain in the same settings page

sections.heading: Is-a.dev Free Domains
paragraphs: Worth spending ten minutes on: is-a.dev gives you a real custom domain — username.is-a.dev — completely free, pointed at your GitHub Pages site.

In other words: It is the fastest path from user.github.io/repo to a name that looks like an actual domain. You request the subdomain, add a CNAME record, and the platform handles the certificate. There is no invoice, ever.
No signup wall, no credit card — just a README and some patience.
bullets: Request yourhandle.is-a.dev in the is-a.dev app
Add the provided CNAME record to your repo's Pages settings
Wait a few minutes for propagation

sections.heading: Automate the boring parts
paragraphs: The short version: Anything you do twice by hand should become a script. That's the entire discipline of free automation.

Concretely: A cron expression, a webhook, or a scheduled workflow costs nothing to run and buys back an hour every week. Start with one small automation — a nightly backup, a feed check, a deploy on push — and add more only when the first one proves itself.
The links in the sources section go straight to the primary docs.

faq.question: Is cloudflare pages free tier actually free?
faq.answer: The honest answer: is-a.dev gives you a real custom domain — username.is-a.dev — completely free, pointed at your GitHub Pages site. Keyless public endpoints can get throttled if you hammer them, so batch your requests and cache what you fetch.

faq.answer: Cloudflare Pages is a free static hosting platform with a global CDN and preview deploys for every pull request. Treat that as the working assumption and re-check the docs once a quarter.
